# LibreBugBounty 2.0.1 “Moneta”

Moneta 2.0.1 turns the existing workspace into a continuously maintained case
inventory. Old findings are rechecked in parallel on a configurable cadence,
browser screenshots remain isolated evidence, and a new health panel makes the
background workers observable.

## Highlights

- **Parallel stock rechecks:** four supervised workers recheck open and
  wont-fix cases after the configured interval — 14 days by default. Claims
  are atomic and leased, interrupted runs recover on their own, errors retry
  after the configured backoff, and cases from the same domain stay spaced by
  at least one hour. A catch-up command can pull every stale slot due at once
  and burn down the backlog with a configurable local worker fleet.
- **Configurable cadence:** the recheck interval (1–90 days) and error
  backoff (1–30 days) live in Settings. Shortening the interval immediately
  pulls future normal slots forward to “last check + new interval”, while
  error backoffs and live worker claims stay untouched.
- **Status & health:** Settings shows whether the recheck and screenshot
  workers are alive, how many rechecks are due now, scheduled, or paused for
  manual review, the next due time, and current screenshot queue counts
  including failures — no terminal needed.
- **Visual evidence only when it matters:** the headless technical pass stays
  parallel and takes no screenshots. A result change or a new
  `inconclusive`/`error` observation queues a separate screenshot for review,
  keeping the technical observation and the visible evidence auditable as
  different records.
- **Four isolated screenshot lanes:** headed captures run in four Playwright
  containers, each with its own Xvfb display. Queue insertion and job claims
  remain safe, but long browser captures no longer wait behind one global
  worker.
- **Screenshot backfill:** `app:screenshot:missing` recognizes cases without
  screenshot evidence and cases whose stored image file has become unreadable.
  Existing active jobs are never duplicated.
- **Clearer automatic outcomes:** a browser-observed `fixed` result is
  applied directly and leaves the recheck scope. Only unclear outcomes require
  manual review.
- **No overlapping review work:** a case in manual checking pauses automatic
  rechecks, including the selection-to-claim race. Its assessment restores the
  normal cadence, and screenshot backfill keeps at most one active job per
  case.

## Upgrading

1. Create and verify a complete [workspace backup](https://github.com/tfgrass/librebugbounty/blob/v2.0.1/BACKUP.md)
   first.
2. Stop DDEV, update this checkout to `v2.0.1`, and run `ddev start`. Startup
   installs the locked dependencies, applies the `nextDueAt` migration, and
   starts four recheck workers plus four screenshot workers.
3. The first start after upgrading creates additional Playwright sidecars. On
   a small machine, reduce the number of `screenshot-worker-*` entries in
   `.ddev/config.yaml` and the matching `playwright-shot-*` services in
   `.ddev/docker-compose.playwright.yaml`; do not point multiple workers at
   the same headed sidecar.
4. Existing cases, observations, assessments, screenshot jobs, and evidence
   are retained. If stored image files were previously lost, queue
   replacements:

   ```bash
   ddev exec php bin/console app:screenshot:missing --limit=1000
   ```

**Cadence note:** 14 days is the new default, but slots that already exist
keep their old timing until their next completed check. To pull older cases
forward immediately, run the catch-up command once — its default threshold
already matches 14 days:

```bash
ddev exec php bin/console app:recheck:catch-up --execute --workers=16
```

For rollback, restore the matching pre-upgrade database and artifacts
together, then check out the previous application version.

## Scope

LibreBugBounty remains a local, single-user reflected-XSS workspace without
authentication or multi-user permissions. Keep the web and Playwright services
local. Disclosure emails and report submission remain manual.
